title: Canada Ties C$1.6B Stake in Cohere to New Job and Computing Targets
summary:
The Canadian government is tying its C$1.6 billion investment in AI developer Cohere to the creation of 1,000 new technical jobs and C$1.7 billion in domestic computing expenditures by 2030. The stake is part of a Series E funding round targeting total capital of C$7 billion at a C$35.7 billion valuation, which the company describes as the largest private financing round in the history of Canadian startups. The raise is led by Schwarz Group and includes support from Nvidia.

Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that the funding is a security investment to ensure Canada achieves tech sovereignty and avoids dependence on AI providers in the U.S. and China. The capital will be used to build frontier models and expand Cohere's ecosystem, which is currently pursuing a combination with Aleph Alpha and an acquisition of cybersecurity firm AISLE. However, the valuation has drawn criticism from some observers who note that Cohere's models have scored between 6 and 9 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, trailing behind rivals such as xAI's Grok, which scored 34.
